To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the self-sufficiency of a rural household in the production and purchase of fruits and vegetables has a significant effect on consumption behavior.

(1) rural households that produce fruits or vegetables, but do no purchase them, are not price sensitive in their consumption of fruits or vegetables; (2) rural households that purchase but do no produce fruits or vegetables are price sensitive in their purchases of fruits or vegetables.

households that produce and purchase fruits and vegetables exhibit the highest level of self-sustainability, households that purchase but do no produce exhibit the highest level or responsiveness, and households that produce but do not purchase are the most price inelastic and the most income elastic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of self-sufficiencies on fruit and vegetable consumption.
the effect of household self-sufficiency on the consumption of fruits and vegetables in the rural households.

the effect of household self-sufficiency on consumption behavior, and the results suggest that the level of household self-sufficient in the production/purchase decision of fruits and vegetables is a significant determinant of household consumption behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
households that produce but do not purchase fruits and vegetables are more sensitive to income effects than households that purchase fruits and vegetables.

the consumption behavior of households that produce and purchase fruits and vegetables is significantly influenced by implicit income effects, and the consumption behavior of those that purchase fruits and vegetables, and do not produce, is significantly influenced by both implicit income and implicit price effects.
households that are self-sufficient in the production of fruits and vegetables are less price responsive than are those that do not produce fruits or vegetables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
households with different levels and patterns of self-sufficiencies in the production and/or purchase of fruits and vegetables exhibit different consumption patterns.
the self-sufficiency level of a rural household has a significant effect on the consumption behavior of that household.
the self-sufficiency level is important to consider when analyzing consumption patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-sufficiency is an important factor in the determination of fruit and vegetable consumption patterns in rural China.
self-sufficiency is an important factor in determining the consumption behavior of China's rural households.
the consumption behavior of China's rural households varies across households with different levels.
